items.gist: The three powers icchā, jñāna, and kriyā are set out, and the pure inert svarūpa is distinguished within the trika universe.
Bhedas among mantramaheśas and related levels are fifteenfold, though not fully treated; the sutra on jāgradāditā is cited.
Distinction arises within the tattva net, with sixteen kṣaṇas measured across thirty-six angulas and graded from paramādvaita to grāhya.
From the third kṣaṇa a six-kṣaṇa nirvikalpa Śiva phase appears, followed by a middle six-kṣaṇa parāpara phase.
Devīs move through the first and second six-kṣaṇa groups, while an increasing excellence is noted among them.
Some hold a seven-and-seven division in subtle cognition, though the text questions verbal elaboration.
The prāṇa-based process is fifteenfold, and reduction of tuṭis brings reduction of vikalpa and clarity of the non-conceptual.
An analogy of forgetting pain illustrates vikalpa reduction, and attention in grāhya-grāhaka cognition is praised as fruitful.
In Śivāveśa two tuṭis remain: one full and pure, the other Śiva-Śakti, all-knowing and all-acting.
Kallaṭa's verse is cited, and the first tuṭi is all-one, while mantras and devīs from the third tuṭi onward yield siddhis through attention.
More tuṭis mean distance and effort, while fewer tuṭis mean nearness to Śiva and absence of effort.
People commonly mistake nearness, and even what is near can appear far in the manner discussed.
Consciousness is not sequential like a seed-sprout; it is full everywhere, and laya occurs in the Śiva seed.
By this method one quickly becomes Bhairava, and the prāṇa distinction is hidden in the khecarī cakra.
Five states are named, and where there is one pramātā, jāgradādi must follow, as shown by Śambhu's grace.
Jāgrat is defined through adhiṣṭheya and adhiṣṭhātṛ, with the fourfold pramātṛ-meya-māna-pramā structure.
The appearance of blue and its adhiṣṭhātṛ relation is examined to clarify jāgrat.
In jāgrat, abuddha, buddha, prabuddha, and suprabuddha are distinguished as four grades.
Each jāgradādi state has a fourfold form, and the meya ground is primary among jāgrat states.
